brand.name: Ember & Oak Coffee Co.
brand.shortDescription: A neighbourhood roastery and coffee bar in downtown Dakar, pouring single-origin coffee since 2021.

hero.eyebrow: Now roasting: Ethiopia Guji, Medium roast
hero.heading:
Slow roasted.
Warmly poured.
hero.subheading: We roast in small batches, twice a week, and pour every cup like it's the only one we're making today.

highlights.title: Small-batch roasting
highlights.description: Beans roasted on-site in 12kg batches, never more, so every bag is within two weeks of the drum.

highlights.title: Direct-trade sourcing
highlights.description: We buy from four family farms we visit every year, and we publish the price we pay them.

highlights.title: A place to stay a while
highlights.description: Big tables, reliable Wi-Fi, and no clock-watching. Bring your laptop or your book club.

about.heading: A café built around the roast, not the logo
about.intro: Ember & Oak started as a Saturday market stall with a 1kg sample roaster and a folding table. Four years on, the roaster is bigger, the table is a counter, and the Saturday-only part is the only thing that changed.
body: We're a two-person roastery that grew into a café because people kept asking where they could sit down and drink the coffee, not just buy the bag.
Every roast is logged: origin, altitude, process, and the curve we ran to get there. Ask any barista and they can tell you why the Guji tastes different this week than it did last month.
We're not trying to be the biggest café in town. We're trying to be the one where the person behind the counter remembers your order.

milestones.label: First roast
milestones.detail: 1kg sample roaster, a Saturday market stall, and a lot of trial batches.

milestones.label: First storefront
milestones.detail: A 40m² corner space with a 5kg drum roaster and six seats.

milestones.label: Direct trade
milestones.detail: First farm visit to Guji, Ethiopia. Began paying and publishing above-market prices.

milestones.label: Today's space
milestones.detail: Moved into our current roastery-café, seating 28, with the roaster visible from every table.

footer.note: Roasted, brewed, and built with care in Dakar.
